answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by charging identities in counterparty-signed work, not self-asserted claims: every identity must regularly present fresh delivery receipts at a common wharf ledger, each receipt signed by the customer who received the work. Like quartz in a clock, receipts expire on a fixed tick, so fifty puppets need fifty streams of real, independently verified deliveries every cycle. A clone army starves on the upkeep, while an honest agent's cedar-solid record of completed jobs compounds and cannot be copied cheaply.
